# pdf-to-einvoice

> Turns an existing invoice PDF into an EN 16931 e-invoice (ZUGFeRD / Factur-X, German "E-Rechnung") without changing how the PDF looks: the invoice data is attached as CII XML and the file becomes a PDF/A-3. The same data can be written as an XRechnung 3.0 for German public bodies. TypeScript library, CLI, MCP server and a browser app. Everything runs locally; no API key, no upload. MIT licence.

Install with `npm install pdf-to-einvoice`, or run without installing: `npx pdf-to-einvoice <command>`.

```ts
import { check, createEInvoice, extractText, guessFromText } from 'pdf-to-einvoice';

const text = await extractText(pdfBytes); // text of the PDF, row by row
const draft = { ...guessFromText(text) /* number, dates, IBAN, tax IDs, totals */ };
const { findings } = check(draft, { pdfText: text }); // what is missing, wrong, or not on the PDF
const { pdf, xml } = await createEInvoice({ pdf: pdfBytes, invoice: draft }); // throws InvoiceError while errors are open
```

XRechnung, for an invoice to a German public body: `createXRechnung({ invoice, syntax })` returns `{ xml, findings, totals }`, plain XML in UBL (default) or CII; `createEInvoice({ pdf, invoice, profile: 'xrechnung' })` puts that XML into the PDF. `check(draft, { rules: 'xrechnung' })` reports what XRechnung asks for on top; both create functions run it.

Command line: `read <pdf> --json`, `schema`, `check <data.json> --pdf <pdf> [--rules xrechnung]`, `create <pdf> <data.json> [-o out.pdf] [--profile xrechnung]`, `xrechnung <data.json> [--syntax ubl|cii] [-o out.xml]`, `validate <einvoice.pdf>`, `xml <einvoice.pdf>`, `mcp`.

MCP server: `npx -y pdf-to-einvoice mcp` (stdio). Tools: `read_invoice_pdf`, `check_invoice`, `create_einvoice`, `create_xrechnung`, `validate_einvoice`, `read_einvoice_xml`.

Rules for an assistant converting an invoice:

- You act for the invoice issuer. A recipient cannot turn a received PDF into a valid e-invoice.
- Copy values exactly as printed on the PDF. Never invent a missing value: ask the user.
- The XML is the legally binding part. Show the findings and get the user's confirmation before creating the file.
- Required: `number`, `issueDate` (YYYY-MM-DD), `seller` and `buyer` with `name` and `country` (two-letter code), `seller.vatId` or `seller.taxNumber`, at least one line with `name`, `quantity`, `unitPrice` (net) and `vatRate`, and `dueDate` or `paymentTerms` when an amount is due.
- `vatCategory`: `S` VAT charged; `AE` reverse charge (EU business customer, needs `buyer.vatId`); `K` intra-community supply of goods (needs `buyer.vatId`); `G` export of goods outside the EU; `O` not subject to VAT (e.g. service for a business outside the EU); `E` exempt (e.g. German small business, § 19 UStG); `Z` zero rated. Every category except `S` and `Z` has `vatRate` 0 and needs `vatExemptionReason`, the sentence printed on the invoice.
- `totals` (`net`, `vat`, `gross`, `due`) are the sums printed on the PDF. A contradiction with the calculated totals is an error: fix the data, do not drop the totals.
- No discounts on document level yet: enter them as a line with a negative quantity.
- XRechnung only for a German public body or when the user asks for it. It needs on top: `buyerReference` (the Leitweg-ID, which the buyer names: ask for it, never make one up), `seller.contactName`, `seller.phone`, `seller.email`, `buyer.email`, and `city` and `postalCode` of both parties. An intra-community supply (`K`) cannot be written as XRechnung.
- Output: a hybrid PDF with CII in the Factur-X / ZUGFeRD profile EN 16931 or XRECHNUNG, or plain XML as XRechnung 3.0 in UBL or CII. Not tax or legal advice.
